Menzel2020.claim: European phenological records show warming-related advances and distinctions between climate-driven phenophases and farmers’ activities; generative periods shortened in agricultural crops.
Menzel2020.placement: Introduction paragraph 2; Discussion climate development versus management adaptation
Menzel2020.limits: Does not validate the present model’s start gate, leaf ranks, flowering or terminal stage.

Bonecke2020.claim: German winter wheat growth stages occurred earlier over the study record, while phase durations did not change uniformly: stem elongation differed from the other developmental phases.
Bonecke2020.placement: Introduction paragraph 2; Discussion timing advance versus interval length
Bonecke2020.limits: Historical phenological data were linked to experiments; this is not disease-specific evidence or validation of retained thresholds.

Martre2015.claim: Across 27 wheat models, accuracy in grain yield or grain protein concentration had little relationship to accuracy in preceding in-season variables; ensemble estimates improved overall performance.
Martre2015.placement: Discussion empirical endpoint support and model uncertainty
Martre2015.limits: A crop-model ensemble differs from the current three-GCM ensemble driving one disease model; do not conflate them.

Asseng2011.claim: Temperature variability and high-temperature-induced senescence during grain filling can substantially alter wheat production in simulation experiments.
Asseng2011.placement: Discussion lower Mediterranean disease does not imply improved total productivity
Asseng2011.limits: Abiotic wheat response, not STB damage, and not a damage-to-yield conversion.

Sparks2014.claim: Global potato late-blight risk initially increased and subsequently declined as planting dates shifted to cooler seasons, illustrating the importance of crop-calendar responses.
Sparks2014.placement: Introduction paragraph 2; Discussion interpretation and management scope
Sparks2014.limits: Prior crop-calendar/disease coupling means the current novelty must be the shared-support factorial attribution, not the first recognition of host calendar effects.

Singh2023.claim: Climate change acts on pathogen evolution, geographic distributions and host–pathogen interactions; crop-phenology and pathogen-development models can yield pathosystem-dependent disease impacts, with standardized data gaps limiting quantitative forecasts.
Singh2023.limits: Review provides framing, not external validation of the current model’s outputs.

Garrett2006.claim: Climate effects span infection, population adaptation and ecosystem processes, and pathosystem characteristics complicate scaling individual infection probabilities to wider impacts.
Garrett2006.limits: Use as conceptual background rather than evidence of the current numerical result.

Waggoner1987.claim: Healthy-area duration integrates healthy leaf area through time; healthy-area absorption additionally accounts for intercepted radiation, making the physiological basis distinct from a symptom-percentage integral.
Waggoner1987.placement: Introduction paragraph 3; Discussion functional canopy endpoints
Waggoner1987.limits: Examples concern several crop pathosystems and do not establish a universal linear conversion to wheat yield. No DOI verified; use official archival URL.

Savary2006.claim: Pathogen injury, crop damage and economic loss form a sequence involving distinct biological and decision processes; the injury–damage relationship carries uncertainty.
Savary2006.placement: Introduction paragraph 1 and 3; Discussion production exposure
Savary2006.limits: Do not relabel the manuscript’s fixed symptom proxy as physiological or economic damage solely on this basis.

Pietravalle2003.claim: English wheat field data supported separate models for STB presence above a severity threshold and STB severity, with rainfall during stem elongation entering the severity model.
Pietravalle2003.placement: Introduction paragraph 2; Discussion symptom occurrence versus accumulated impact
Pietravalle2003.limits: Correlative empirical weather models do not validate the present latent-state process model; no universal weather coefficients are implied.

Robert2004.claim: Cultivar differences in STB timing apparent from sowing disappeared when time was expressed from flowering; the work also explicitly linked canopy layers, measured photosynthesis and senescence to crop growth effects.
Robert2004.placement: Introduction paragraphs 2–3; Discussion host-relative timing and functional canopy
Robert2004.limits: Strong antecedent: do not claim discovery of host-relative epidemic timing. Its leaf-photosynthesis parameters and natural-senescence correction cannot be transferred to the current normalized proxy without calibration.

Bernard2013.claim: Controlled experiments on adult wheat showed a nonlinear STB latent-period response to measured leaf temperature and differences among pathogen isolates and leaf layers; leaf temperature can differ from air temperature.
Bernard2013.placement: Introduction paragraph 2; Methods forcing qualification; Discussion missing canopy microclimate
Bernard2013.limits: Its latent period used time to 37% of final sporulating area, distinct from first visible symptoms. Do not import numerical durations or optima as direct validation of the retained model.

Minoli2022.claim: Global crop-model experiments separated no adaptation, timely adaptation and delayed adaptation of sowing dates and cultivars, showing that fixed and adaptive growing-period assumptions answer different management scenarios.
Minoli2022.placement: Discussion fixed calendar and adaptation scope
Minoli2022.limits: This paper’s simulated adaptation gains are not evidence of feasible gains for the current disease model or all European farms.

Asseng2013.claim: A standardized wheat intercomparison found climate-impact differences arising from crop model structures and parameters, with crop-model uncertainty exceeding downscaled-GCM uncertainty in that experiment.
Asseng2013.placement: Discussion structural uncertainty versus selected GCM spread
Asseng2013.limits: The relative uncertainty contributions are experiment-specific; do not assign their numerical partition to the current study.

Asseng2015.claim: Testing 30 wheat models against temperature experiments, including warming treatments, exposed poorer model accuracy at high temperatures and benefits of evaluation across contrasting thermal conditions.
Asseng2015.placement: Discussion independent response evaluation and extrapolation
Asseng2015.limits: The global yield sensitivity is not a disease coefficient and should not be used to convert proxy days into grain losses.

Ploton2020.claim: Spatially random train–test partitions can exaggerate predictive performance in spatially structured ecological data; spatial blocks or exclusion buffers address a different extrapolation setting.
Ploton2020.placement: Methods monitoring evaluation design; Discussion validation limits
Ploton2020.limits: Forest biomass case study, not a prescribed 50-km buffer for STB. Earlier same-field conditioning still changes the information setting even when outer training locations are excluded.

Bebber2013.claim: Recorded crop pests and pathogens shifted polewards on average after 1960, with substantial differences among taxonomic groups.
Bebber2013.placement: Introduction paragraph 1, emergence and geographic responses
Bebber2013.limits: This does not show an STB-specific range shift in Europe or verify disease magnitude under future climate.

Fisher2012.claim: Emerging fungal diseases threaten managed and natural ecosystems, and human activity can intensify dispersal and opportunities for pathogen evolution.
Fisher2012.limits: Overlaps the existing Fones2020 framing; select only where it adds historical context, not to inflate citation counts.

Knutti2013.claim: CMIP5 local projection spread persisted despite substantial model development; greater model complexity did not by itself remove projection uncertainty.
Knutti2013.limits: Does not by itself establish a probabilistic interpretation or quantify uncertainty for this selected three-model CMIP6 ensemble.

guidelines.initial_submission_style: Free Format; no strict initial formatting requirement, all essential manuscript elements required. Specific formatting follows acceptance.
guidelines.reference_style_finding: The current guideline page contains no explicit alphabetical ordering or mandatory reference-format prescription. A consistent author–year style and alphabetized bibliography are editorial choices, not a newly verified mandatory GCB rule.
guidelines.maps_disclaimer_exact: map lines delineate study areas and do not necessarily depict accepted national boundaries
guidelines.data_sharing: Mandatory data sharing; data access for peer review must be provided on request.
guidelines.content_inspected: Current publisher guideline page, original-research requirements and formatting instructions, retrieved 2026-10-23.

eligibility_notes.prohibited_publishers: MDPI and Frontiers were neither intentionally searched/opened nor used as evidence; incidental search results were skipped.
eligibility_notes.journal_of_experimental_botany: Publisher homepage explicitly describes JXB as a top-ranking plant-science journal, owned by the Society for Experimental Biology; its broad physiological scope and original wheat-STB study make Robert2004 suitable. No claim of Nature-family status is made.
eligibility_notes.phytopathology: APS official page describes Phytopathology as the premier international journal for fundamental and applied plant-disease research.
eligibility_notes.plant_pathology: Society ownership and scope were verified, but this alone does not establish the strict field-top status. The two otherwise very relevant Plant Pathology papers are held out.

editorial_use: Priorities indicate fit, not a citation quota. Avoid adding all three optional broad/abiotic references if their associated claim adds no substantive content. Do not cite any outside paper as validation of the current autonomous model, its physiological interpretation, or grain losses.
